findings.text: issue (blocking): The proposed move does not define an executable binding between an observed successful suite execution and the checkpoint Ship accepts. Git can prove commit contents and ancestry, but an agent-authored checkpoint with matching SHAs has the same observable shape whether the suite ran or was skipped; the current hook dispatches only push-shaped commands (loom-code/scripts/loom_checker.py:3234), and its observed execution is the guarantee being removed (loom-code/scripts/loom_checker.py:3998).
findings.fix: Specify the authoritative branch-end execution-to-checkpoint transition, its enforcement on both supported hosts, and how Ship rejects a fabricated, copied, legacy, or interrupted checkpoint without trusting result fields. Include a negative acceptance case with a schema-valid passing checkpoint for an unexecuted or failing suite. If Git-only state cannot establish execution under the selected trust model, resolve that design contradiction explicitly before implementation.

findings.text: issue (blocking): REQ-1 blocks a missing declaration or unusable command, while the design decision at line 24 preserves existing fallback and error behaviour. Existing resolution accepts absent declarations through build markers (loom-code/scripts/loom_checker.py:3977), and an explicit package-tests: none succeeds without a run (loom-code/scripts/loom_checker.py:4014); the two readings produce different outcomes in adopting repositories.
findings.fix: Define separate outcomes for absent declaration with successful detection, absent declaration without detection, explicit none, malformed argv, missing executable, timeout, and non-zero exit. State whether the existing none exemption is preserved, and align REQ-1 and the UI flow with that decision.

findings.text: issue (blocking): The suite runs before the blind run and adversarial work, but that work currently commits evidence before the final reviewers are dispatched (loom-code/skills/review/SKILL.md:157), including executable regression cases (loom-code/skills/review/SKILL.md:307). The spec does not settle whether those later commits invalidate the tested commit, cause another suite execution, or are exempted, so exactly once against the final implementation commit is not yet executable.
findings.fix: Place the single successful suite execution after all tree-changing branch-end work and before checkpoint creation, or define an equivalent precise ordering. Explicitly invalidate the run on later probe, evidence, nit, command-declaration, or other tracked-content changes; describe retry behaviour and the exact permitted close-record exceptions without introducing general safe-path exemptions.

findings.text: issue (blocking): The current checker does not create a clean worktree at the reviewed commit. It checks the existing working tree for cleanliness (loom-code/scripts/loom_checker.py:4050) and executes the declared command with cwd set to that repository (loom-code/scripts/loom_checker.py:4066); _cmd_push calls it directly without creating another checkout (loom-code/scripts/loom_checker.py:3306).
findings.fix: Correct Current state evidence to distinguish the documented claim from the actual execution directory. Specify whether the candidate will execute at the pinned commit in an isolated checkout or validate and use the existing checkout, including how it prevents HEAD movement and tracked changes during execution.

findings.text: issue (blocking): The baseline count is fixed at two before measurement, but the existing Ship instructions call the push checker explicitly and then state that the host hook runs it again when pushing (loom-code/skills/ship/SKILL.md:238 and :247), in addition to the branch-end run (loom-code/skills/review/SKILL.md:317). A full unchanged workflow therefore has additional execution sites; a two-call replay requires an explicitly narrower scope.
findings.fix: Define the replay start and stop points and whether actual push-hook execution and Ship's preceding test checklist are included. Record the observed baseline invocation count rather than requiring two, then require one candidate execution over that identical scope, equal release verdicts, and lower measured wait.

notes: The corrected reviewed SHA matches HEAD. All five Current state evidence sources were opened; findings above distinguish source text from executable behaviour.

findings.text: issue (blocking): The final snapshot closes only the interval before the PreToolUse checker returns. A package command can launch a detached process that moves the branch or changes the tree after this comparison but before the intercepted named-branch push resolves its source; the committed adversarial case explicitly demonstrates the checker returning success before a delayed mutation.
findings.fix: Make the pushed source immutable across the hook-to-command boundary, for example by requiring and validating an explicit reviewed commit SHA refspec, or move the validation into an atomic push boundary that receives the exact refs. Add a delayed HEAD-moving attack proving that the network operation cannot publish a post-validation commit.

findings.text: issue (blocking): The measurement does not replay either revision's real Ship-to-hook path. It searches Ship prose for one literal and directly runs a synthetic workload once or twice; it never invokes either revision's checker, hook adapter, checkpoint validation, adversarial probes, or release decision, and it constructs the verdict from those synthetic subprocess return codes.
findings.fix: Build the same accepted-checkpoint fixture for both revisions, execute the baseline explicit checker plus hook and the candidate hook through their versioned real entry points, instrument the declared package command, and measure the complete local boundary through the actual checker release or block result.

findings.text: issue (blocking): The report says every repository mutation is blocked, but the branch-end attack catalogue records a deterministic counterexample in which the gate returns success and a detached writer then mutates the reviewed tree. This hides a release-safety gap from the user's acceptance material.
findings.fix: Report the detached-process counterexample as an unresolved limitation and mark Acceptance #1, #2, and #5 not yet satisfied until the hook-to-push race is closed.

findings.text: issue (blocking): The final synchronous HEAD and porcelain snapshot does not contain detached descendants of a successful probe. The committed attack starts a detached writer, observes checker exit 0, and then observes the reviewed tree mutate, so the hook can release the network push before the final state boundary is actually stable.
findings.fix: Run package and adversarial commands inside an isolation boundary that cannot retain writers against the selected repository after the command returns, then verify that boundary has terminated before the final Git snapshot. Convert the detached-writer case into a permanent regression test requiring the checker to block.

findings.text: issue (blocking): The new concurrent-mutation case treats the unsafe release as its expected passing result: it requires checker exit 0 and only afterward confirms mutation. This documents the defect but does not protect the intended fail-closed behavior, and the case has not been graduated into the permanent checker suite.
findings.fix: After fixing process containment, change this case to require a non-zero checker result with the relevant BLOCK rule, graduate it into loom-code/scripts, and record the graduated probe in review.json.

findings.text: issue (blocking): The timing replay does not execute either revision's Ship-to-hook gate. It searches Ship prose for a literal and directly runs a synthetic workload once or twice, then derives release solely from those workload return codes. Consequently the reported local-gate verdict and elapsed boundary exclude checker validation, adversarial probes, repository state checks, and hook dispatch.
findings.fix: Replay an accepted temporary checkpoint through each revision's actual checker and hook entry point, instrument only the resolved package command for invocation counts, and measure monotonically from the simulated Ship push request through the real hook release or block result.

findings.text: issue (blocking): The report says there are no blocking or important functional problems even though the same HEAD adds an executable probe and commit message showing that a detached writer escapes the final check. This could cause the user to accept an unsafe push gate.
findings.fix: Report the detached-writer escape as blocking, change Acceptance 1 and 5 to not-working until the regression is fixed, and regenerate the summary only after the corrected permanent probe passes.

notes: Exact HEAD and merge-base were independently verified; the worktree remained clean and no files were modified.
